newsitem.title: USA: Boeing CEO confident about merger.
newsitem.headline: Boeing CEO confident about merger.

text.p: Boeing Co Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Phil Condit said Friday he was confident the company's planned merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp will close in August as planned.

Condit also told reporters after a luncheon speech that he was confident Boeing would work out its differences with the European Union, which had said it would not approve the merger if Boeing continued exclusive provider relationships with Delta Air Lines Inc and AMR Corp's American Airlines.

Earlier, European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert, who was addressing the National Press Club in Washington D.C., told Reuters the EU would not authorize the merger unless Boeing ended the exclusive provider agreements.
Condit said he had not yet seen Van Miert's remarks, but he insisted the carriers had a choice among jetmakers in a highly competitive market.
"Fundamentally this is a competitive market," Condit said.
"We strive hard to win our competitions and get the right products to our customers," he said. "I think that's what competition's about."
Condit met with Van Miert in March and said further high-level talks were not scheduled until late June or early July.
